```{r setup}
library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)

# Interactive 3D picture of a joint pdf: the domain as a blue floor, the pdf
# as a surface, and an event's volume in orange (top plus walls to the floor)
plotly_pdf_volume <- function(f, x_lim, y_lim,
                              in_domain = function(x, y) rep(TRUE, length(x)),
                              domain_corners,
                              in_event = NULL, event_corners = NULL,
                              z_max, z_ratio = 0.7, n = 121) {
  xs <- seq(x_lim[1], x_lim[2], length.out = n)
  ys <- seq(y_lim[1], y_lim[2], length.out = n)
  grid <- expand_grid(y = ys, x = xs) |>
    mutate(domain = in_domain(x, y),
           height = if_else(domain, f(x, y), NA_real_),
           event = if (is.null(in_event)) 0 else as.numeric(domain & in_event(x, y)))
  as_mat <- function(v) matrix(v, nrow = n, ncol = n, byrow = TRUE)
  grey_orange <- list(c(0, "#9fb8c8"), c(1, "#E89543"))

  # Floor: one flat polygon at height 0 over the domain
  floor_x <- domain_corners[, 1]
  floor_y <- domain_corners[, 2]
  p <- plot_ly(height = 650) |>
    add_trace(type = "mesh3d", x = floor_x, y = floor_y, z = 0 * floor_x,
              delaunayaxis = "z", color = I("#29abe0"), opacity = 0.3,
              hoverinfo = "skip", name = "Possible values (domain)") |>
    add_surface(x = xs, y = ys, z = as_mat(grid$height),
                surfacecolor = as_mat(grid$event), cmin = 0, cmax = 1,
                colorscale = grey_orange, opacity = 0.9, showscale = FALSE,
                name = "Joint pdf",
                hovertemplate = "x = %{x:.2f}<br>y = %{y:.2f}<br>f(x, y) = %{z:.3f}<extra></extra>")

  if (!is.null(event_corners)) {
    corners <- rbind(event_corners, event_corners[1, ])
    for (k in 1:(nrow(corners) - 1)) {
      s <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 40)
      wall_x <- corners[k, 1] + s * (corners[k + 1, 1] - corners[k, 1])
      wall_y <- corners[k, 2] + s * (corners[k + 1, 2] - corners[k, 2])
      wall_top <- f(wall_x, wall_y)
      p <- p |> add_surface(x = rbind(wall_x, wall_x), y = rbind(wall_y, wall_y),
                            z = rbind(0 * wall_top, wall_top),
                            surfacecolor = matrix(1, 2, 40), cmin = 0, cmax = 1,
                            colorscale = grey_orange, opacity = 0.55,
                            showscale = FALSE, hoverinfo = "skip")
    }
  }

  p |> layout(
    showlegend = FALSE,
    margin = list(l = 0, r = 0, t = 0, b = 0),
    scene = list(
      xaxis = list(title = "x"), yaxis = list(title = "y"),
      zaxis = list(title = "f(x, y)", range = c(0, z_max)),
      aspectmode = "manual", aspectratio = list(x = 1, y = 1, z = z_ratio),
      camera = list(eye = list(x = 1.5, y = -1.6, z = 0.9))))
}
```

Each plot below is an interactive 3D picture for an example in the [Lesson 16 slides](16_Independence_conditioning.qmd).

-   **Drag** to rotate, **scroll** to zoom, and **double-click** to reset the view.
-   **Hover** over the surface to see $x$, $y$, and the height $f_{X,Y}(x,y)$.
-   **Blue floor:** the possible values (where $f_{X,Y}(x,y) > 0$).
-   **Orange:** the event. Its volume, from the floor up to the pdf, is the probability we approximate with simulation.
-   **Orange lines:** a *slice* of the joint pdf at one value of $y$. Conditioning on $Y = y$ keeps only that slice.


## Example 1: conditioning on $Y = 1$ {#ex1-slice}

Two draws without replacement from a box with balls 1, 2, and 3 (from Lesson 15). Each stick stands on a pair $(x, y)$, and its height is $p_{X,Y}(x,y)$. The **orange** sticks are the slice $Y = 1$. Conditioning on $Y = 1$ keeps only those sticks, then rescales them so they add to 1: $p_{X|Y}(x|1) = \frac{1/6}{1/3} = \frac12$ for $x = 2, 3$.

```{r}
ex1_pmf <- expand_grid(x = 1:3, y = 1:3) |>
  mutate(prob = if_else(x == y, 0, 1/6),
         stick_color = if_else(y == 1, "#E89543", "#9fb8c8"))

ex1_sticks <- ex1_pmf |>
  filter(prob > 0) |>
  mutate(id = row_number()) |>
  reframe(x = c(x, x, NA), y = c(y, y, NA), z = c(0, prob, NA),
          stick_color = stick_color[1], .by = id)

floor_lines <- bind_rows(
  tibble(x = rep(c(0.5, 3.5, NA), 3), y = rep(1:3, each = 3)),
  tibble(x = rep(1:3, each = 3), y = rep(c(0.5, 3.5, NA), 3))
) |>
  mutate(z = if_else(is.na(x) | is.na(y), NA_real_, 0))

p <- plot_ly(height = 650) |>
  add_trace(type = "mesh3d", x = c(0.5, 3.5, 3.5, 0.5), y = c(0.5, 0.5, 3.5, 3.5),
            z = c(0, 0, 0, 0), delaunayaxis = "z", color = I("#29abe0"),
            opacity = 0.3, hoverinfo = "skip") |>
  add_trace(data = floor_lines, x = ~x, y = ~y, z = ~z, type = "scatter3d",
            mode = "lines", line = list(color = "#bbbbbb", width = 2),
            hoverinfo = "skip")

for (col in c("#9fb8c8", "#E89543")) {
  p <- p |>
    add_trace(data = filter(ex1_sticks, stick_color == col), x = ~x, y = ~y, z = ~z,
              type = "scatter3d", mode = "lines",
              line = list(color = col, width = 10), hoverinfo = "skip") |>
    add_trace(data = filter(ex1_pmf, prob > 0, stick_color == col),
              x = ~x, y = ~y, z = ~prob, type = "scatter3d", mode = "markers",
              marker = list(color = col, size = 6),
              hovertemplate = "(x, y) = (%{x}, %{y})<br>p(x, y) = %{z:.4f}<extra></extra>")
}

p |>
  add_trace(data = filter(ex1_pmf, prob == 0), x = ~x, y = ~y, z = ~prob,
            type = "scatter3d", mode = "markers",
            marker = list(color = "#666666", size = 6, symbol = "x"),
            hovertemplate = "(x, y) = (%{x}, %{y})<br>p(x, y) = 0<extra></extra>") |>
  layout(
    showlegend = FALSE,
    margin = list(l = 0, r = 0, t = 0, b = 0),
    scene = list(
      xaxis = list(title = "x", tickvals = 1:3),
      yaxis = list(title = "y", tickvals = 1:3),
      zaxis = list(title = "p(x, y)", range = c(0, 0.25)),
      aspectmode = "manual", aspectratio = list(x = 1, y = 1, z = 0.7),
      camera = list(eye = list(x = 1.5, y = -1.6, z = 0.9))))
```

## Example 2: volume for $\mathbb{P}(0 \leq X \leq 1, 0 \leq Y \leq \frac12)$ {#ex2-volume}

$X$ and $Y$ are independent, with $f_X(x) = \frac12$ for $0 \leq x \leq 2$ and $f_Y(y) = 3y^2$ for $0 \leq y \leq 1$, so $f_{X,Y}(x,y) = \frac32 y^2$ (the same joint pdf as Lesson 15, Example 2).

```{r}
plotly_pdf_volume(
  f = function(x, y) 3/2 * y^2, x_lim = c(0, 2), y_lim = c(0, 1),
  domain_corners = rbind(c(0, 0), c(2, 0), c(2, 1), c(0, 1)),
  in_event = function(x, y) x <= 1 & y <= 0.5,
  event_corners = rbind(c(0, 0), c(1, 0), c(1, 0.5), c(0, 0.5)), z_max = 1.6
)
```

## Example 3: the joint pdf and its slices {#ex3-pdf}

$f_{X,Y}(x,y) = 18x^2y^5$, for $0 \leq x \leq 1$, $0 \leq y \leq 1$. The orange lines are slices at $y = 0.6$, $0.8$, and $1$. Each slice is $18y^5 \cdot x^2$: a taller or shorter copy of the **same** curve, $x^2$. Rescale any slice to area 1 and you get $f_{X|Y}(x|y) = 3x^2 = f_X(x)$, whatever $y$ is. That is what independence looks like.

```{r}
slice_lines <- expand_grid(y = c(0.6, 0.8, 1), x = c(seq(0, 1, by = 0.01), NA)) |>
  mutate(z = 18 * x^2 * y^5)

plotly_pdf_volume(
  f = function(x, y) 18 * x^2 * y^5, x_lim = c(0, 1), y_lim = c(0, 1),
  domain_corners = rbind(c(0, 0), c(1, 0), c(1, 1), c(0, 1)), z_max = 18
) |>
  add_trace(data = slice_lines, x = ~x, y = ~y, z = ~z, type = "scatter3d",
            mode = "lines", line = list(color = "#E89543", width = 8),
            hovertemplate = "slice y = %{y}<br>x = %{x:.2f}<br>f(x, y) = %{z:.3f}<extra></extra>")
```

## Example 4 (for home): the joint pdf {#ex4-pdf}

$f_{X,Y}(x,y) = 2e^{-(x+y)}$, for $0 \leq x \leq y$ (shown up to 4; it keeps going). The formula splits into $e^{-x}$ times $e^{-y}$, but look at the floor: it is a triangle, not a rectangle. The possible values of $X$ depend on $y$.

```{r}
plotly_pdf_volume(
  f = function(x, y) 2 * exp(-(x + y)), x_lim = c(0, 4), y_lim = c(0, 4),
  in_domain = function(x, y) x <= y,
  domain_corners = rbind(c(0, 0), c(0, 4), c(4, 4)), z_max = 2
)
```

## Example 5: the plane $y = 0.2$ {#ex5-plane}

$f_{X,Y}(x,y) = 5e^{-x-3y}$, for $0 < y < \frac{x}{2}$ (shown up to $x = 6$; it keeps going). The **orange plane** is $y = 0.2$. It only crosses the possible values for $x > 0.4$, and the **dark orange curve** is the slice it cuts out of the joint pdf, $f_{X,Y}(x, 0.2)$. Conditioning on $Y = 0.2$ keeps only this slice. The simulation keeps the simulated pairs in a thin strip around the plane.

```{r}
# Build the surface slice by slice: for each y, x runs from the edge of the
# domain (x = 2y) to 6, so the edge x = 2y stays smooth
f5 <- function(x, y) 5 * exp(-x - 3 * y)
t_vals <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 121)
y_vals <- seq(0, 3, length.out = 61)
x_mat <- outer(y_vals, t_vals, function(y, t) 2 * y + t * (6 - 2 * y))
y_mat <- outer(y_vals, t_vals, function(y, t) y + 0 * t)
z_mat <- f5(x_mat, y_mat)

slice_02 <- tibble(x = seq(0.4, 6, by = 0.02), y = 0.2) |>
  mutate(z = f5(x, y))

plot_ly(height = 650) |>
  add_trace(type = "mesh3d", x = c(0, 6, 6), y = c(0, 0, 3),
            z = c(0, 0, 0), color = I("#29abe0"),
            opacity = 0.3, hoverinfo = "skip") |>
  add_surface(x = x_mat, y = y_mat, z = z_mat,
              colorscale = list(c(0, "#9fb8c8"), c(1, "#9fb8c8")),
              opacity = 0.85, showscale = FALSE,
              hovertemplate = "x = %{x:.2f}<br>y = %{y:.2f}<br>f(x, y) = %{z:.3f}<extra></extra>") |>
  add_surface(x = matrix(c(0, 6, 0, 6), 2, 2, byrow = TRUE),
              y = matrix(0.2, 2, 2), z = matrix(c(0, 0, 5, 5), 2, 2, byrow = TRUE),
              colorscale = list(c(0, "#E89543"), c(1, "#E89543")),
              opacity = 0.45, showscale = FALSE, hoverinfo = "skip") |>
  add_trace(data = slice_02, x = ~x, y = ~y, z = ~z, type = "scatter3d",
            mode = "lines", line = list(color = "#d35400", width = 10),
            hovertemplate = "slice y = 0.2<br>x = %{x:.2f}<br>f(x, 0.2) = %{z:.3f}<extra></extra>") |>
  layout(
    showlegend = FALSE,
    margin = list(l = 0, r = 0, t = 0, b = 0),
    scene = list(
      xaxis = list(title = "x", range = c(0, 6)),
      yaxis = list(title = "y", range = c(0, 3)),
      zaxis = list(title = "f(x, y)", range = c(0, 5)),
      aspectmode = "manual", aspectratio = list(x = 1.4, y = 1, z = 0.7),
      camera = list(eye = list(x = 1.5, y = -1.6, z = 0.9))))
```
